claims.text: The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA has a dual-phase FCC+B2 microstructure.
The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy exhibits high ductility.
Aging AlCoCrFeNi2.1 at approximately 600°C induces maximum brittleness and sharply reduces elongation.
Aging AlCoCrFeNi2.1 at approximately 750°C restores ductility.
Aging at 600°C produces L12 ordered domains with near-stoichiometric Ni3Al ratios within the FCC matrix.
Aging at 600°C produces jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries.
Near-stoichiometric Ni3Al-like L12 ordering maximizes the antiphase-boundary energy in the FCC matrix.
The increased APBE at 600°C inhibits cross-slip of partial dislocations.
Suppressed cross-slip forces deformation to proceed by planar slip.
Planar slip bands accumulate at serrations in jagged B2/FCC interfaces.
Jagged B2/FCC boundary serrations act as stress concentrators.
The accumulation of planar slip and stress at boundary serrations causes intergranular or transgranular fracture.
At 750°C, thermal energy lowers the L12 chemical-order parameter.
Lower L12 order at 750°C reduces APBE and permits dislocation cross-slip.
At 750°C, B2/FCC interfaces become smoother or develop ductile transition zones.
Ductility is recovered at 750°C because reduced ordering and altered interfaces remove the high-APBE, serration-controlled deformation network.
The brittle state occurs when the L12 order parameter exceeds an unspecified critical value and the B2/FCC interfaces are jagged.
L12 superlattice diffraction intensity measured by SAED can be used to quantify the order parameter S.

contradictions.description: The central hypothesis requires high L12 ordering together with jagged interfaces, but falsification condition (3) treats high ordering at 750°C with retained ductility as sufficient to reject ordering as the primary driver. That result could remain compatible with the coupled hypothesis if the 750°C interfaces were no longer jagged or had developed ductile transition zones.
